Directly reconstructed spectral majorization reduction to the scalar simplex and strict-convex KKT (μ_i=(λ_i−τ)_+, trace 1), making the nearest-state map independent of 1<p<∞. On traceless 2×2 and 3×3 Hermitians the S_p norms at every p (n=2), respectively S4 alone (n=3), are proportional to S2; Hilbert projection gives constant 1, fixed distinct states make it sharp. For n≥4 derivative of ||diag(1,1,−2,0)+t diag(1,1,1,−3)||_p^p is p(2−2^(p−1)), vanishing only at 2; the three-active-coordinate threshold map removes the Z direction and produces strict expansion. For n=3 independently differentiated the noncommuting Y=[[1,0,1],[0,−1,0],[1,0,0]], Z=diag(1,1,−2): (1/p) derivative of ||Y+tZ||_p^p equals (φ^(p−3)+φ^(3−p))/√5−1 and vanishes only at 2,4. At the simple-spectrum Aδ the divided-difference derivative converges to Y. Independent numerical derivatives agree at nine exponents; 80 random-projection checks and six finite expansive witnesses corroborate but do not prove the universal bounds. The theorem proves only qualitative strict expansion; no exact expansive constants or endpoints.
